source_gaps: The prior Windows link (find-my-downloads-in-windows-10) redirects to a page titled 'File Explorer in Windows' that has no download-specific steps. Windows 11 guidance is therefore thin: the page says to search from a folder like Downloads and lists Downloads under Quick access, but gives no direct step for opening Downloads from Quick access. Chrome: the page does not mention Ctrl+J or a downloads icon shortcut, so none is used. Chrome Linux default location is on the page but not used, because no task names Linux.

source_refs.title: File Explorer in Windows | Microsoft Support
source_refs.section: Restore known folders if you have unpinned them
source_refs.applicability: Windows 11 and Windows 10 (the page's Applies To line)
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Select and hold (or right-click) on the folder you wish to restore and select Pin to Quick access from the context menu.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Windows 11, if you have unpinned a folder such as Downloads from Quick access: 1. Select Start > File Explorer, or select the File Explorer icon in the taskbar. 2. Select Home in the left navigation pane. 3. Select the Up arrow from the navigation buttons available to the left of the address bar. 4. Select and hold (or right-click) on the folder you wish to restore and select Pin to Quick access from the context menu.
